chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-03.proposition: Analogical predication permits one simple divine reality to ground distinct attributions of knowledge and power without identifying the corresponding creaturely properties.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source independently presents analogy as necessary for simplicity and denies that divine knowledge and power are univocally predicated creaturely properties.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-05.proposition: Divine simplicity excludes real intrinsic distinctions in God while allowing grounded conceptual distinctions among attributes and contingent extrinsic predications concerning creatures.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source positively defines simplicity's scope by distinguishing mind-grounded attribution from real intrinsic differentiation and by expressly permitting extrinsic contingency and change.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-06.proposition: Divine aseity supports simplicity because intrinsic components would make God's being or properties depend on realities not identical with the metaphysically ultimate source.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source advances this directly from God's complete and radical independence and status as the first, metaphysically ultimate source of reality.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-08.proposition: The threat composition poses to aseity is explanatory grounding: even if God could ground alleged parts, the unity making those parts one composite would ground God.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source supplies a freestanding explanatory-grounding objection to divine composition by locating dependence in the unity of the parts rather than in the parts alone.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: A Latin Trinitarian model reconciles simplicity with real personal distinction by identifying each person and procession-relation with the divine essence while distinguishing persons through opposed relations.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source positively proposes the Latin model, rejects a community account, and grounds personal distinction in relations rather than compositional constituents.

chunk-002:c002-04.proposition: The Son is identical with begottenness relationally and with the divine essence absolutely, while the directedness of that relation adds no positive ontological item to God.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source independently explains the metaphysics of the Son's relation to the Father and expressly denies that relational towardness is an additional positive entity.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: Changing contingent truths alter extrinsic knowledge predications without changing God's intrinsic positive reality, so they do not introduce acquired knowledge or potentiality in God.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source affirmatively distinguishes intrinsic divine reality from the extrinsic truth of what is known and locates temporal differences in creatures rather than in God.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: God's contingent knowledge consists in his intrinsic intellect and causal efficacy, while differences among temporally varying true knowledge attributions are entirely extrinsic.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source provides a positive metaphysical account of divine knowledge by grounding it in intellect and causality while assigning its contingent differentiation to creaturely history.
